stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes an AWS Lambda function that writes each order to a small Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During traffic spikes, so many copies of the function connect at the same time that the database fails. The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time. Clients must receive the result of each order in the API response, and the clients already retry any request that fails. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time
Clients must receive the result of each order in the API response

options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 50, and keep the API Gateway integration pointed at the function as it is today.
options.why: Reserved concurrency can [cap traffic rates to downstream resources](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-per-function-concurrency-control), so Lambda runs 50 copies or fewer and throttles the rest, which the clients retry.

options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 50 on a published alias of the function, and point the API Gateway integration at that alias.
options.why: Provisioned concurrency is no ceiling, because Lambda can scale the function [above and beyond your provisioned concurrency setting](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-scales-beyond-setting).

options.text: Place an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and the function, and set the maximum concurrency of the event source mapping to 50.
options.why: It limits the copies, but API Gateway answers when the message is in the queue, so clients no longer receive the order result in the API response.
options.misconception: believes that a queue in front of a function still returns the result of the function to the API caller

options.text: Move the code into containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service that runs no more than 50 tasks.
options.why: It can hold the limit, but moving the whole API to containers is far more to build and run than one setting on the function.

explanation: The database fails because too many copies connect at once, so the fix is a ceiling on one function. AWS says to configure reserved concurrency to [limit how high your function can scale](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-bp-reserved-protects-downstream). Lambda throttles the requests above the ceiling, the clients retry them, and the setting [incurs no additional charges](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-reserved-concurrency-no-charge). The API stays synchronous, so each client still gets its order result.
takeaway: Reserved concurrency caps one function, and provisioned concurrency prepares environments without a cap.
twin: If the stem said "After quiet periods, the first requests take several seconds" instead: provisioned concurrency on an alias, because it keeps functions [ready to respond in double-digit milliseconds](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-snapstart-vs-pc-guide).
say: I'd set reserved concurrency to fifty, because it caps the function, so the database never sees more than fifty copies.

stem: A company stores customer uploads in an Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon S3 invokes an AWS Lambda function for each new object. Some uploads are malformed, and the function fails on every attempt to process them. Today, these failed events are retried and then lost. The operations team must keep a record of each failed event, with details about the failed invocation, as an object in a separate S3 bucket. The team must receive each record as soon as possible after the first failure. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
keywords: as an object in a separate S3 bucket
as soon as possible after the first failure

options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose the separate S3 bucket as the destination.
options.why: Lambda can send records of asynchronous invocations to [An Amazon S3 bucket (on failure only)](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-destination-targets), as a record with details about the failed invocation.

options.text: Set the maximum retry attempts in the asynchronous invocation configuration of the function to 0, so that a failed event is not retried.
options.why: The retry count can be set [between 0 and 2](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-retry-attempts-0-to-2); at 0, the first failure goes to the destination at once.

options.text: Configure an Amazon SQS standard queue as the dead-letter queue of the function, and read the failed events from that queue.
options.why: A dead-letter queue can be an [Amazon SQS queue or an Amazon SNS topic](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-dlq-sqs-or-sns), so no record reaches the S3 bucket.

options.text: Configure an on-failure destination for asynchronous invocations of the function, and choose an Amazon SNS FIFO topic as the destination.
options.why: A FIFO topic is an [unsupported destination type](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-destination-fifo-unsupported) for asynchronous invocation records, so no record arrives.
options.misconception: believes that any Amazon SNS topic can receive invocation records

options.text: Add error handling code to the function that writes each failed event and its error message as an object to the separate S3 bucket.
options.why: It works, but custom error code in the function is more to build and maintain than two settings in the asynchronous invocation configuration.

explanation: Amazon S3 invokes the function asynchronously. After a failure, Lambda tries [two more times](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-default-two-retries), and then [Lambda discards it](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-discard-then-destination) unless a destination keeps it. An on-failure destination can be an S3 bucket, which receives a record with details about the invocation, and a retry count of 0 sends the record after the first failure.
takeaway: Failed asynchronous events go to an on-failure destination, which can be an S3 bucket; 0 retries sends them at once.
twin: If the stem said "must keep each failed event in an Amazon SQS queue" instead: a dead-letter queue also fits, because it can be an [Amazon SQS queue or an Amazon SNS topic](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-dlq-sqs-or-sns).
say: An on-failure destination writes each failed event with its invocation details to the S3 bucket, and zero retries sends it right after the first failure.

stem: A company runs an AWS Lambda function that answers product search requests. At the start of every invocation, the handler downloads the same 300 MB reference file from an Amazon S3 bucket, which makes each request slow. The file changes once a week, and the company accepts that an execution environment keeps using an old copy for a few hours. The function serves a steady load of about 20 concurrent requests that does not grow. Every request must be fast, including the first request in each execution environment. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort? (Select TWO.)
keywords: the handler downloads the same 300 MB reference file
including the first request in each execution environment

options.text: Move the download out of the handler into the initialization code, so that the download runs once when Lambda prepares each environment.
options.why: Initialization code runs before the handler and [is not run again](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-static-init-reuse-connections) when an invocation uses a warm execution environment, so the download happens once per environment.

options.text: Store the reference file in an environment variable of the function, and read the variable at the start of each invocation.
options.why: All environment variables of a function together are limited to [4 KB](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-env-vars-size), which is far too small for the 300 MB file.
options.misconception: believes that environment variables can hold large data files

options.text: Cache the file in the /tmp directory from the handler, and download it again only when the file is not in /tmp yet.
options.why: The copy in /tmp [remains when the execution environment is frozen](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-tmp-transient-cache), but the first request in each environment still downloads the file.
options.misconception: believes that a cache that the handler fills also makes the first request in a new environment fast

options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 20 on an alias of the function, and point the callers of the function at that alias.
options.why: Provisioned concurrency keeps [pre-initialized execution environments](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-scales-beyond-setting), so the initialization code has run before the first request arrives.

options.text: Rebuild the search service as containers on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, with tasks that load the file at startup and keep it in memory.
options.why: It works, but rebuilding the service on containers is far more development than one code change and one function setting.

explanation: The download repeats because it runs in the handler. Code outside the handler runs once per environment, because [Lambda can reuse the environment](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-warm-start-environment-reuse) for later requests. Provisioned concurrency runs that code before requests arrive, so the function [does not exhibit cold start behavior](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-not-latest-no-cold-start). Lambda [terminates execution environments every few hours](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-environment-not-persistent), so a new copy arrives within hours of a change.
takeaway: Load a large shared file in initialization code, and add provisioned concurrency so that even the first request in an environment is fast.
twin: If the stem said "slow first requests in a new environment are acceptable" instead: the initialization code alone fits, because it [is not run again](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-static-init-reuse-connections) on a warm start.

stem: A company processes clickstream records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream with an AWS Lambda function. The event source mapping uses the default settings. However, one malformed record makes the function fail, and processing of that record's shard stops for days while the other shards continue. The company wants to keep the full content of each failed record for later analysis and keep each shard moving. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: The event source mapping uses the default settings
keep the full content of each failed record

options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue on the function, so that Lambda moves the malformed record to an Amazon SQS queue after its retries end.
options.why: A function's [dead letter queue](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-dlq-after-retries) receives asynchronous events after their retries; a stream mapping keeps failed records in its own on-failure destination.

options.text: On the event source mapping, turn on bisect batch on function error, set a retry limit, and add an Amazon S3 bucket as the on-failure destination.
options.why: [BisectBatchOnFunctionError](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-stream-bisect-batch-on-error) isolates the bad record, the retry limit ends the loop, and an [Amazon S3 bucket](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-kinesis-on-failure-destination-targets) destination receives the entire invocation record.

options.text: Raise the parallelization factor of the event source mapping, so that other concurrent batches from the same shard move past the malformed record.
options.why: More batches for each shard keep no copy of the failed record, and Lambda [stops processing additional records in a shard](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-kinesis-in-order-stops-on-error) after an error.
options.misconception: believes that more concurrent batches for each shard skip a record that keeps failing

options.text: Add code to the function that catches parse errors, writes each malformed record to an Amazon S3 bucket, and returns success for the batch.
options.why: It works, but parsing and copying code in the function is more to build and maintain than three settings on the event source mapping.

explanation: With the default settings, [failed records are retried until the record expires](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-kinesis-max-retry-attempts), so a bad record can block its shard for [up to one week](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-kinesis-bad-record-block-one-week). Bisect batch isolates the record, a retry limit stops the loop, and an S3 on-failure destination keeps the whole invocation record while the shard moves on.
takeaway: A poison record in a stream needs bisect batch, a retry limit and an on-failure destination on the mapping.
twin: If the stem said "an Amazon SQS standard queue" instead: a redrive policy on the source queue, because the [visibility timeout and redrive policy](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-queue-esm-retry-set-on-queue) decide where failed messages go.
say: Split the failed batch, cap the retries and send the bad record to an S3 on-failure destination, so the shard keeps moving.
